review.summary:
Independent phase-22 review at reviewed source 78c4cd64… ("Red Team target configuration and filtering support"). I verified the artifacts rather than the prose, and the phase's declared milestones are genuinely implemented.

Milestone 22.1 (connection unions + five response declarations): the overlay appends exactly one reviewed tail to each of two frozen union nodes — `s010462` → `Variant5(red_team_management::VertexAIConnectionParams)` and `s010504` → `Variant3(red_team_management::MultiTurnClientSessionConfig)` (generated.rs:172559, 172270; schema_graph `s010504` variants confirmed as legacy prefix + new tail). Because all four connection-params families (`s010789/s010821/s010824/s010829`) share those two union types (generated.rs:12885, 162494, 171980, 184380), REST/streaming/WebSocket/request variants are all covered by two nodes rather than four divergent copies. Appending at the tail cannot narrow old acceptance, and the legacy prefix is pinned positionally (`verify_union_pins`, red_team_management_models.py:265-281, with prefix/tail/missing regressions at test_red_team_management_models.py:138-158). `client_session` is opt-in: the vendor `default: client_session` is deliberately not compiled into a ZodDefault (red_team_management_models.py:158-162; asserted at test_red_team_management_models.py:133-136), so `{}` still resolves to the legacy stateless branch and `{"type":"client_session"}` to the new one (tests/red_team_management_models.rs:67-93). All five target operations are driven end-to-end through `RedTeamTargetsClient` with a mock transport across 5 provider shapes × 4 auth shapes × both response modes, asserting operation names, methods, `/mgmt-plane` paths, masked GET vs unredacted mutations, and `!Debug.contains(SECRET)` (tests/red_team_management_contracts.rs:337-445), and each row is recorded with per-field vendor/SDK presence-nullability comparison, required-field equality and an explicit `comparisonLimit` (red_team_management.py:637-675; compatibility-decisions.json:4788-4814).

Milestone 22.2 (filters): `profiling_status` is validated against a generated vocabulary, not a hand-written list — `TARGET_PROFILING_FILTER_VALUES` is derived from `components.schemas.ProfilingStatusFilter.enum` with empty/duplicate/non-string guards (red_team_management_models.py:241-244 → models/red_team_management.rs:360), and I independently confirmed that domain (NOT_STARTED, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, FAILED) and the DRAFT/ACTIVE `status` domain in the pinned vendor YAML (mp-openapi.yaml:3640-3647, 5942-5946, 371-380). `query()` is the single query builder; `list_pages` pre-validates then clones all options and overwrites only `skip` (targets.rs:339-369), and `list_items`/`list_all` route exclusively through it, proven on the wire with exact query-pair counts across all four surfaces (contracts.rs:451-525). Undeclared values are refused before token acquisition and dispatch (`provider.calls == 0`, empty transport log, contracts.rs:526-544). Legacy `status` is transmitted unchanged with no invented mapping, and every management response `profiling_status` stays `Patch<String>` (generated.rs:175036 et al.), so INIT/QUEUED/PARTIALLY_COMPLETE survive by construction. NOTICE and crates/scm-sdk/NOTICE both attribute pan.dev 582e3054 / 0.86.0 alongside the data-plane revision.

Milestone 22.3-22.4: four optional typed projections preserve every formerly accepted raw value (generated.rs:162501-162632 decodes into `Patch` and re-inserts the raw value on failure, skipping the duplicate key on collision; pinned at contracts.rs:558-588 and models.rs:95-117), a packaged offline example runs on both compilers (`cargo run --example red_team_management` exit 0 on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0), and `--require-through-phase 22` now demands real artifacts: manifest `usedForGeneration`, byte hashes for twelve generated/test/notice/vendor inputs, agreement between the overlay and union-extension ledgers, public models present in the runtime graph, all 13 wire-test function names present, and a fail-closed offline live boundary (red_team_management.py:698-749). Phase 23-25 still fail closed (line 759).

Evidence is executed, not asserted: docs/reviews/phase-22-attempt-01.checks.json is bound to the reviewed source hash, `passed: true`, 42 commands all exit 0 with real durations and captured output, including five `scripts/check-rust.py` matrices (fmt, check --all-targets, clippy -D warnings, test, test --examples, doc) on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0, and docs/checks/phase-22-rust-1.89.0-red-team.json shows the new management tests actually passing on MSRV. `native_operations`/`native_exports`/`qualification` all report liveVerified 0, matching the phase-22 offline boundary; the dependency audit is fresh with an unchanged lockfile and policy.

Weaknesses are small and mostly documentation/test-precision. The one thing that currently blocks advancement is governance rather than code: the declared `connection-compatibility` chunk has no accepted review at this source (attempt-03 is an `invocation_failed` receipt, attempt-04 has a prompt and checks snapshot but no record), so `tools/review_phase.py:355-368` will correctly reject the phase while the latest chunk record remains bound to 20d8e7c6…. Seven low findings also remain open in current source, four of them explicitly deferred to phase 23 by docs/reviews/phase-22-attempt-03-followups.md. Categories 9.5/9/9/9.5/9.5 = 46.5/50; no blocker or high finding.

findings.description: The declared chunk `connection-compatibility` has no accepted review at the reviewed source. Its attempt-03 receipt is `{"status":"invocation_failed","reason":"invalid_output"}` (docs/reviews/phase-22-chunk-connection-compatibility-attempt-03.failed.json:6), and attempt-04 has only a prompt and a checks snapshot (docs/reviews/phase-22-chunk-connection-compatibility-attempt-04.checks.json:3, same source 78c4cd64… and checked_at 15:52:13 as this phase receipt) with no `.json` record. The latest matching record is attempt-02, bound to source 20d8e7c6… at 46.5/50. `tools/review_phase.py:326-368` therefore refuses advancement: the stale-source fallback requires an accepted *fifth* chunk review, and the sibling chunks (`target-filtering` 46/50, `typed-connections` 45.5/50) are accepted at attempt 3 on the current source while this one is not. The phase's own milestone text requires chunk reviews before the phase review (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:218). This is an evidence-ordering gap, not a code defect, and docs/PHASES.md:170 explicitly treats an in-flight prompt as not-yet-failed.
findings.required_fix: Let the connection-compatibility attempt-04 invocation finish and record an accepted current-source chunk review (every category >=8, total >=42/50, no blocker/high) at 78c4cd64…, then advance; if it is rejected or fails to launch, fix the cause, rerun the phase checks and use the remaining attempt budget before any phase advancement. Phase acceptance must not be recorded while that chunk's latest record is bound to 20d8e7c6….

findings.description: The plan-mandated migration rustdoc ends with "None is mapped to `NOT_STARTED` or any other filter automatically." On a field typed `Option<String>`, that sentence reads naturally as a claim about `Option::None` (i.e. that an unset filter defaults to NOT_STARTED), which is the opposite of the implemented behavior: `query()` omits the parameter entirely when the option is `None` (targets.rs:79-86, proved by the empty-query assertion at targets.rs:423-427). The intended meaning is "none of the retained response values (INIT, QUEUED, PARTIALLY_COMPLETE) is mapped", which is exactly the plan's "Preserve; do not map to NOT_STARTED" decision (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:156-159). This was raised in the target-filtering attempt-03 review and deferred, but it is the one sentence where ambiguity changes caller behavior.
findings.required_fix: Reword targets.rs:38-40 so the subject is explicit, e.g. "No response value is automatically mapped to `NOT_STARTED` or any other filter value, and an unset filter sends no `profiling_status` parameter."

findings.description: The struct rustdoc says invalid values "fail before authentication or dispatch, so their validation errors do not carry a dispatched operation name" but never names the observable error kind. `query()` validates skip/limit/search/adapter_uuid/target_type/status/profiling_status in one pass and returns a bare `crate::Error::new(crate::ErrorKind::Validation)` (targets.rs:83) with no parameter indication and `operation() == None`, so a caller matching on errors from list/list_pages/list_items/list_all has no in-crate statement of what to match.
findings.required_fix: Name the kind in the rustdoc at targets.rs:15-16, e.g. "Any unsupported query value, including an undeclared `profiling_status`, fails as `ErrorKind::Validation` before authentication or dispatch; no request is sent and the error carries no operation name or caller value."

findings.description: In `all_five_operations_preserve_declared_sensitive_response_shapes` the expected value for all five operations is `validation::parse("TargetResponseSchema", expected, mode)` — the same validator the client path exercises. A validator defect that dropped or rewrote a field would be invisible because both sides of the assertion shift together. Validator-independent raw anchors exist in adjacent tests (contracts.rs:67-69, 163-167; models.rs:21, 32) but not per operation row, so the plan's "every row requires both response modes, raw and typed round-trip fixtures" (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:141) is only partially met per row.
findings.required_fix: In the `Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults` iteration of the five-operation matrix, additionally assert `serde_json::to_value(actual).unwrap() == expected` against the hand-written response document so each of the five rows has a validator-independent raw oracle.

findings.description: In `unknown_discriminators_and_required_vertex_types_stay_validated` the inner loop iterates `Mode::Request`, `Mode::Response` and `Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults`, but for the `{"type":"client_session","future":null}` payload the `else if mode != Mode::Request` branch asserts nothing in request mode, so one of six iterations parses and silently discards its outcome. Either the request-mode result for that payload is a contract worth pinning (this is a response root being parsed in request mode) or the mode should not be iterated for that case.
findings.required_fix: Assert the intended `Mode::Request` outcome explicitly for the client_session payload, or restrict the mode list for that case so no loop iteration is unasserted.

findings.description: `structuralChecks.regexSources` records only the four frozen baseline patterns, while crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1058-1066 now implements seven (the three reviewed Vertex request patterns). The gap is enforced, not silent — tools/generate_models.py:897 requires the native pattern table to equal `REGEX_SOURCES | MANAGEMENT_REGEX_SOURCES`, and validation.rs:1219 fails closed on an unknown pattern source even in response mode — but the ledger is derived from the frozen inventory only (generate_models.py:915), so the published model contract understates the implemented request-validation surface with no pointer to where the overlay-owned patterns live.
findings.required_fix: Either add an explicitly labelled overlay-owned list (e.g. `managementRegexSources`) derived from `red_team_management_models.PATTERNS`, or add a one-line note in the ledger stating that overlay-owned request patterns are recorded in contracts/red-team-management-model-overlay.json and the vendor compatibility decisions.

findings.description: `management_runtime_evidence()` hash-binds the overlay/union ledgers, targets.rs, both Rust test files and the Python overlay test, but omits crates/scm-sdk/examples/red_team_management.rs — the milestone 22.3 packaged consumer deliverable. Deleting the example would be caught (scripts/check-rust.py runs `cargo run --example red_team_management`), but reducing its body to a trivial `main` would pass every gate while the recorded evidence still claims a packaged consumer exercise. The repository already has a stronger precedent for binding example content (tools/test_g10_release.py `test_rust_additions_resolve_to_declarations_and_the_packaged_example`).
findings.required_fix: Add `crates/scm-sdk/examples/red_team_management.rs` to the `management_runtime_evidence` path list, or assert its required API usage (Vertex builder, `Variant5`/`Variant3`, `TargetCreateRequestResponseMode::REALTIME`, both response modes, `profiling_status`) the way the G10 example check does.

findings.description: The authoritative plan still instructs "Extend `TargetConnectionType` with `VERTEX_AI`, `N8N`; extend `ResponseMode` with `REALTIME`" (and docs/PHASES.md:136 repeats "enums" generically). The implementation extends the schema-graph vocabularies `s012061`/`s012067` and names the new values on `TargetCreateRequestConnectionType`/`TargetCreateRequestResponseMode`, deliberately leaving the frozen TypeScript-parity enums at their old values with `Unknown(String)` (generated.rs rustdoc injected at generate_models.py:1062-1066; asserted at tests/red_team_management_models.rs:135-164). The decision is sound and is recorded in the overlay ledger `enumCompatibility`, but a reader of the plan gets contradictory guidance about which public enum carries the new variants, and the phase-24 changelog obligation inherits that ambiguity.
findings.required_fix: Update the plan's connection/union section and the phase-24 changelog obligation to state the frozen-parity versus schema-bound enum split explicitly, naming `TargetCreateRequestConnectionType`/`TargetCreateRequestResponseMode` as the types that declare `VERTEX_AI`, `N8N` and `REALTIME`.

findings.description: The management projection addendum documents typed-over-raw precedence and that wrong-type values remain in extension storage, but never states the consumer-observable relocation: for `basic_username`, `basic_password`, `audio_request_json` and `audio_curl`, a representable value is now removed from the extension map and placed in the typed `Patch` field (generated.rs:162503-162521 removes the key and only re-inserts it when the typed decode fails). Wire round-trips are unchanged (contracts.rs:174-193), but existing consumer code that read `params.extensions.get("audio_curl")` now sees `None` for a well-typed value. This is inherent to the approved design, yet it is the kind of transition the plan requires to be recorded for consumers (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:108).
findings.required_fix: State explicitly in the management addendum (and carry it into the phase-24 changelog beside the Unknown→named-variant transitions) that a representable value now populates the typed projection field and is no longer present in `extensions`, while unrepresentable values and the serialized wire form are unchanged.

limitations: Read-only review with Read/Glob/Grep only: I executed no command, made no network call and could not recompute any SHA-256, including the supplied checks digest fa4af024…. Pass/fail conclusions rest on docs/reviews/phase-22-attempt-01.checks.json, whose recorded source_sha256 equals the reviewed SHA and whose entries contain real invocations, exit codes, captured stdout/stderr and plausible durations; I verified the command list against tools/check_phase.py:187-270 rather than observing the runs.

docs/phase-status.json still records phase 22 as in_progress with all three chunks "pending", empty `reviews`, pending milestones and no `review_findings_disposition`. That bookkeeping is written by tools/review_phase.py at advancement, so I did not treat it as a defect, but it means no in-repo record yet links the accepted target-filtering (46/50) and typed-connections (45.5/50) reviews or the disposition of their low findings; docs/reviews/phase-22-attempt-0N-fixes.md and -followups.md are the only such record.

All evidence is offline or local-transport. No live service acceptance exists or is claimed for this phase (liveVerified 0 by design); nothing here certifies that the service accepts or rejects any particular status, profiling_status, Vertex configuration or client_session payload. The SDK's strict client-side filter vocabulary is a reviewed plan decision (plan lines 147-150) agreeing with the pinned 0.86.0 spec, not a proven upstream contract, and an upstream fifth filter value would fail closed at the reviewed source hash pending review.

The local gate exercises red-team, red-team+json-unification and json-unification feature sets on two compilers. The default/minimal/all matrix, packaged consumer builds and real old-consumer source compatibility are explicitly phase 23 scope, and `cargo run --example` plus the absence of a models-on/red-team-off build mean `TARGET_PROFILING_FILTER_VALUES` (#[cfg(feature = "red-team")]) is safe by construction but unverified in that configuration here. Local passing records do not prove the remote 48-job matrix ran.

There is no independently derived corpus for the management projections, union tails or enum values: all management behavioural evidence is hand-written Rust fixtures plus the Python overlay regressions. The frozen TypeScript oracle cannot know new vendor fields, the boundary is disclosed in docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:34 and docs/reviews/phase-22-attempt-02-fixes.md:17-21, and building a management equivalent of the derived corpora is a phase 23 obligation, so I recorded it as a limitation rather than a phase-22 deficiency.

I opened no credential or tenant-registration material and inspected nothing outside this repository; I did not read anything under .local (the oracle commands that reference .local/typescript were assessed only from the receipt). Later-phase operations marked planned, phase 23 qualification and phase 24 changelog/release obligations were not treated as missing phase-22 deliverables, and the historical 0.2.2 receipts were not treated as new-source acceptance.
